claim: The JSDoc "slightly more time" for the first-chunk timeout understates a 2x difference (120000ms vs 60000ms).
raw: Critical (Medium) — "slightly more time" understates a 2x difference. `fetcherService.ts:301` (JSDoc block 299–302 on `SSE_FIRST_CHUNK_TIMEOUT_MS`). 120000ms vs 60000ms is exactly **double**, not "slightly." Also a comment-rot magnet

claim: Correctness silently relies on the undocumented Web-Streams invariant that destroy() resolves the in-flight read() as done; add a comment documenting the coupling.
raw: Low — correctness depends on an undocumented Web-Streams invariant. `fetcherService.ts:344-346` (and `break`-then-throw at `358-373`). The design silently relies on `destroy()` resolving the in-flight `read()` as `{done:true}` rather than rejecting. Add a one-line comment documenting the coupling.

claim: It is unestablished whether the retry pipeline classifies the new StreamIdleTimeoutError as retryable; transient hangs that used to recover could become terminal failures.
raw: Low / design question — retryability of the new error at call sites. `messagesApi.ts:596`, `responsesApi.ts:537`, `stream.ts:323`. if the retry layer only matches known network-error shapes, transient hangs that used to eventually recover could become terminal failures.

claim: void stream.destroy().catch(()=>{}) swallows async rejection but not a synchronous throw from destroy() inside setTimeout (would become uncaught).
raw: Negligible — sync-throw in the timer callback. `fetcherService.ts:346`. `void stream.destroy().catch(() => {})` swallows async rejection but not a *synchronous* throw from `destroy()` inside `setTimeout` (would become uncaught). Theoretical only

raw: Test note (brief): coverage is good; minor gaps — no assertion pins the numeric `timeoutMs`, and no test for the token-cancellation path through the wrapper.

raw: FINDING 1 — MEDIUM — Empty catch swallows every `destroy()` rejection with zero logging. `fetcherService.ts:346`. `void stream.destroy().catch(() => { })` discards cancel-algorithm rejections — no log, no error ID.

claim: If the reader rejects the pending read on cancel, iterator.next() rejects and the post-finally throw at line 371 is never reached, so StreamIdleTimeoutError is never thrown.
raw: FINDING 2 — HIGH (conditional) [Inference] — Intended `StreamIdleTimeoutError` silently replaced if the reader rejects on cancel. If the underlying stream rejects the pending read on cancel, `iterator.next()` rejects and line 371 is never reached — the distinct error is never thrown.

claim: An awaited rejection in finally (iterator.return?.()) replaces whatever was propagating, masking the fall-through timeout throw or a real error.
raw: FINDING 3 — MEDIUM [Inference] — `finally` block can mask the pending timeout throw. `fetcherService.ts:368`. An awaited rejection in `finally` (`iterator.return?.()`) replaces whatever was propagating — would supersede the fall-through `if (timedOut) throw` and any real error. Wrap in try/catch.

claim: No log or telemetry is emitted when the watchdog trips; no way to distinguish first-chunk from idle timeouts or attribute a hung-stream incident.
raw: FINDING 4 — MEDIUM — No log or telemetry emitted when the watchdog actually trips. `fetcherService.ts:344-347` and `:371-373`. no `logError`/`logForDebugging`/`logEvent`, no error ID, no way to distinguish first-chunk (2 min) from idle (60 s) timeouts in telemetry. Emit log + telemetry

claim: If destroy() took the else branch stream.cancel() while still locked it rejects with TypeError (swallowed), leaving the read hung forever with no error.
raw: FINDING 5 — LOW [Inference] — Swallowed `stream.cancel()` on the unlocked branch could leave the read hung with no error. it rejects with `TypeError` (swallowed by Finding 1's catch), and the pending `read()` never unblocks → generator hangs forever with no error.

claim: AsyncIterableObject delivers buffered completions before the stored error, so a consumer treating an earlier finishReason as terminal could ignore the trailing timeout error.
raw: One caveat: `AsyncIterableObject` delivers buffered completions *before* the stored error, so the timeout arrives after earlier partial completions — a consumer treating an earlier `finishReason` as terminal could ignore the trailing error (worth confirming consumer-side, outside this diff).
